1.web: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.
1.asv: And when he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was noised that he was in the house.

2.web: Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.
2.asv: And many were gathered together, so that there was no longer room for them, no, not even about the door: and he spake the word unto them.

3.web: Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.
3.asv: And they come, bringing unto him a man sick of the palsy, borne of four.

4.web: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.
4.asv: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed whereon the sick of the palsy lay.

5.web: Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
5.asv: And Jesus seeing their faith saith unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins are forgiven.

6.web: But there were some of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
6.asv: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

7.web: “Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
7.asv: Why doth this man thus speak? he blasphemeth: who can forgive sins but one, even God?

8.web: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
8.asv: And straightway Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, saith unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

9.web: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’
9.asv: Which is easier, to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

10.web: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—
10.asv: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (he saith to the sick of the palsy),

11.web: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
11.asv: I say unto thee, Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thy house.

12.web: He arose, and immediately took up the mat, and went out in front of them all; so that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”
12.asv: And he arose, and straightway took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.

13.web: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
13.asv: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

14.web: As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.
14.asv: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting at the place of toll, and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

15.web: He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
15.asv: And it came to pass, that he was sitting at meat in his house, and many publicans and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

16.web: The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
16.asv: And the scribes of the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and publicans, said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?

17.web: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
17.asv: And when Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.

18.web: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”
18.asv: And John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting: and they come and say unto him, Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

19.web: Jesus said to them, “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.
19.asv: And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

20.web: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.
20.asv: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.

21.web: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
21.asv: No man seweth a piece of undressed cloth on an old garment: else that which should fill it up taketh from it, the new from the old, and a worse rent is made.

22.web: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
22.asv: And no man putteth new wine into old wine-skins; else the wine will burst the skins, and the wine perisheth, and the skins: but they put new wine into fresh wine-skins.

23.web: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields, and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.
23.asv: And it came to pass, that he was going on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears.

24.web: The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”
24.asv: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?

25.web: He said to them, “Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
25.asv: And he said unto them, Did ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry, he, and they that were with him?

26.web: How he entered into God’s house when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”
26.asv: How he entered into the house of God when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the showbread, which it is not lawful to eat save for the priests, and gave also to them that were with him?

27.web: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
27.asv: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

28.web: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
28.asv: so that the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath.
